grade.first_issue: The proof invokes without explicit justification that every positive solution of \(3v^2-2u^2=1\) belongs to the displayed Pell orbit.
grade.summary: The transformations, congruence restrictions, closed forms, and final identity \(2x+2y+1=v_k^2\) are correct. The only omission is the completeness of the Pell parametrization; this follows routinely by dividing \(v\sqrt3+u\sqrt2\) by \(\sqrt3+\sqrt2\) and applying the standard unit classification in \(\mathbb Z[\sqrt6]\).
strengths: Correctly derives the Pell-type equation and proves the desired square identity for every solution in the stated orbit.
Correctly identifies that the original integrality conditions force the Pell index to be even.

errors.description: Completeness of the asserted Pell parametrization is not explicitly established.
